solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Strips off article back in bed?

indicators.note: back tells us the whole string of pieces is read from end to start

parts.note: to strip off is to peel, as a skin is peeled away
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether undressing and an item of clothing tossed back belong in the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PEELSA into the answer; the question mark flags that being in bed is only one way to be sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in bed is usually sleeping, so the phrase loosely stands for that state.

clue.text: Hold up kiosk

definitions.meaning: a small booth or stand selling goods at a market

explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to delay; a stall is also a small trading booth, two separate senses.

clue.text: Train engine's first to run about on time

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it
about tells us the two words to run are shuffled around

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A steam engine sets off on schedule at the head of a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the anagram of 'to run'; 'on' is a link meaning followed by. 'Train' looks like a railway word but means a retinue.
explanation.definitionFit: A train can mean a retinue of followers, the attendants accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Send up giving stick in benefit

indicators.note: in tells us the stick goes inside the benefit

parts.note: pay is what you receive as a benefit of work
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the payment of welfare by a caning.
explanation.definitionFit: To send up is a British idiom for mocking by imitation, which is what a spoof does.

clue.text: Obliged really to confine basket case

indicators.note: to confine means one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: indeed means really, as an intensifier

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone is truly forced to lock up a hopeless person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'basket case' is a slang phrase for a wreck, but here 'case' takes the outer letters B and T of basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Being obliged to someone means owing them, so one is in their debt.

clue.text: Fan must start in line to see musician

indicators.note: to fan is to spread out, so the letters are spread and rearranged

explanation.surface: A devotee has to begin queueing to catch a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like the devotee in the queue but is the verb that spreads the letters of MUST START IN LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Any player of a musical instrument is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Girl's rear in trousers ends giving bulges

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, with the possessive S

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the trouser ends
ends asks for the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: the rear is the end of something

explanation.surface: A woman's backside in her trousers ends up swelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes T and S from trousers, and 'in' puts END between them for TENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell outward from pressure inside is to bulge, as a stomach does.

clue.text: Shady place for bender?

definitions.meaning: a leafy arbour or shelter in a garden
one who bows, that is who bends at the waist

explanation.definitionFit: A bower is a shaded garden retreat, and comically one who bows, a person who bends.

clue.text: Irritation indeed seen within damaged retina

indicators.note: seen within puts one piece inside the other
damaged tells us the letters of retina are broken and rearranged

parts.note: yes is an emphatic agreement, like indeed

explanation.surface: An eye irritation is visible in a hurt retina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' signals the anagram, and 'seen within' places the word for indeed inside it, just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, sore eyes from overuse are a form of discomfort or soreness.

clue.text: Improves following terribly acute burns

indicators.note: following places the piece improves after the anagram
terribly signals the letters of acute are badly jumbled

parts.note: rises means goes up, improves

explanation.surface: A patient's condition gets better after severe sharp pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To cauterise a wound is to seal it by burning, so the verb means burns.

clue.text: Soaked taking on hard grind

indicators.note: taking on means accepting something inside

parts.note: wet means soaked
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Drenched and facing tough, tedious toil.
explanation.definitionFit: To whet a blade is to sharpen it on a stone, which grinding does.

clue.text: Submerge to catch large fish

indicators.note: to catch puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a ship that founders sinks below the waves
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: An angler goes under in order to land a big fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The flounder is a flatfish, a specific species of fish.

clue.text: Time with grass inside for mistakes

indicators.note: inside puts one piece within another

parts.note: an era is a period of time
to rat is to inform, as a grass does in British slang

explanation.surface: A period of time with weeds growing in it produces errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is British slang for an informer, so here RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed printing errors, so the word means mistakes.

clue.text: Singer Gaga making comeback …

indicators.note: making comeback means the word is read backwards

parts.note: gaga means infatuated, avid

explanation.surface: The pop star Lady Gaga returns to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaga' looks like the pop star, but it means keen, AVID.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female singer, especially of opera.

clue.text: Inject syringe's centre and roughly clean out

indicators.note: centre asks for the middle letter of the word
roughly signals the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Inject with the middle of a syringe and then scrub it out carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes I, the middle letter of syringe; 'roughly' turns CLEAN OUT into NOCULATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To inoculate is to give a vaccine, typically by injection.

clue.text: … song, crazy chick covering Queen single

indicators.note: covering means the outer pieces enclose the inner pair

parts.note: mad means crazy
a chick is slang for a girl, a gal
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
I, the Roman one, means single

explanation.surface: A crazy young woman sings with a lone queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues from the previous clue, but each clue is solved separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for several voices, popular in Renaissance times.

clue.text: Noted compiler's left a note, oddly

parts.note: the crossword setter refers to himself as I am, so I'M
port is the left side of a ship
taken as written

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in odd places of the word

explanation.surface: A setter mentions that he left a strange message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes N and T from note.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone noted is eminent and well known, the same as significant.

clue.text: Make public record on waste

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the record comes first

parts.note: a disc is a vinyl record
to lose an opportunity is to waste it

explanation.surface: Publicise a record about squandering resources.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something hidden is to make it known to everyone.

clue.text: Funny man's about average with old content

indicators.note: content means contained, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
the median is a kind of average

explanation.surface: A clown is roughly ordinary and happy with former times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads as happy, but means held inside: O sits inside C MEDIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian is a male entertainer who makes people laugh.

clue.text: Mine includes mid-evening drink

indicators.note: includes means one piece holds another

parts.note: a pit is a mine

indicators.note: mid- asks for the middle letter of the word it is joined to

explanation.surface: A coal mine has a pub break in mid-evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint is a measure of beer, the usual drink in a British pub.

clue.text: Holy place seeing religious leader bathed in glow

indicators.note: bathed in tells us one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to shine is to glow

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sanctuary where a cleric is lit up in light.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrine is a sacred site devoted to a saint or deity.

clue.text: Rugby club endlessly rough

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union

indicators.note: endlessly takes the last letter off

parts.note: a stick is a club

explanation.surface: A rugby club plays without stopping in a rough manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic means simple and rough in workmanship, like country furniture.

clue.text: Newspaper with article on crime

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the other piece

parts.note: the is the definite article
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs a story about a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, a British daily paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is stealing, a specific crime.

clue.text: Metaphor is maybe conveying proverb

indicators.note: conveying means carrying the answer within the words

explanation.surface: A figure of speech might carry a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphorism is a short witty saying, which is a kind of maxim.

clue.text: Crack one found around top of vase

indicators.note: found around means one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: sole means one, only

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter in a down clue

explanation.surface: A crack is found running around the rim of a vase.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a puzzle or code is to work it out.

clue.text: Naked apart from burlesque ending

parts.note: bar means except, apart from

indicators.note: ending takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Nude but for the end of a strip show.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare and naked both mean without clothing.

clue.text: First using mouth to swallow one drink

indicators.note: to swallow means take something inside

parts.note: orally means by the mouth
I, the Roman numeral, is one
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: First, gulp one shot by mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally means at first, in the beginning.

clue.text: Feeling that is not heartless after broadcast

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the broadcast

parts.note: sent means transmitted, broadcast
IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Emotion that is not cold after a programme airs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves the N and T of not.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentient being is capable of sensation, able to perceive.

clue.text: Respect sweetheart before engagement's over

indicators.note: before places the sweetheart in front of the other piece

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is E

indicators.note: over means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a meet is a sporting engagement, plus S

explanation.surface: Admire your lover before the engagement ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem means high regard, the same as respect.
